teaser: Two people stand behind the same name, so to speak: a 1, who leads, and an ISFJ, who tends. At a farmers market stall, you are the one who set up the tent alone before dawn and are now handing a neighbor's child a free apple because she looked tired. The 1 wants the stall to be yours, run your way, answering to no one. The ISFJ wants everyone fed, remembered, and comfortable before the till is even opened. This crossing is not a contradiction so much as a quiet argument between running the thing and running it for others, settled a little differently every market day.
excerpt: The clink of cafeteria trays in a hospital waiting area, and you are the one who already found the vending machine, already knows which coffee the other person takes.
